topic: The proposed MOVE-to-CA fix is a
canonical_claim: The proposed MOVE-to-CA fix is a CAS-aware `clonePart` path that stages the whole part in one `ContentAddressedTransaction`; the generic per-file cross-disk copy path is insufficient.

topic: Whole-part atomicity sites such as freeze
canonical_claim: Whole-part atomicity sites such as `freeze`, restore-from-backup, and B58 projection commits remain single-`commit` transactions because this design deliberately introduces no `precommit` phase.

topic: Verbatim table-level and mountpoint files are
canonical_claim: Verbatim table-level and mountpoint files are treated as an immediate autocommit class: writes are durable on finalize and deletes or moves remain durable at call time, avoiding a second timeline for those files.

topic: The MOVE-to-CA design was reframed as
canonical_claim: The MOVE-to-CA design was reframed as one whole-part `ContentAddressedTransaction` threaded through the move, plus a layer-1 parser fix so the final part identity is used instead of `moving`; the earlier claim that a transactional copy would lack full build semantics was rejected.

topic: Review finding №12's call-time mutation of
canonical_claim: Review finding №12's call-time mutation of durable refs is by design: `renameParts` is the commit point and rollback compensates with new operations over committed disk state, but `removeDirectory` must discard staged entries when removing a part before commit.

topic: For CA part moves, the crash-atomic
canonical_claim: For CA part moves, the crash-atomic design uses a transient `moving/<part>` reference prefix: `clonePart` commits under the moving reference and the mover later repoints it to the final reference, so startup cleanup can reclaim an orphaned moving reference.; Publishing a cloned CA part directly under the final `<part>` reference before the mover swaps it is rejected because the final directory already exists and a crash can leave a committed final reference that moving-reference cleanup cannot reclaim.

topic: The production INSERT topology contract
canonical_claim: The production INSERT topology commits one `ContentAddressedTransaction` per part, so cross-part batching must occur at the `MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts` seam rather than inside `ContentAddressedTransaction::commit`. A plain INSERT performs one `ContentAddressedTransaction::commit()` per part with `parts.size() == 1`, so inner-loop parallelism cannot improve INSERT; cross-part concurrency must be introduced above the disk transaction.

topic: The phased engine uses one precommit
canonical_claim: The phased engine uses one precommit ledger batch, one flattened cross-part upload wave, and one promote ledger batch; a 500-part INSERT is expected to reduce about 1026 serial ref-log PUTs to about two.

topic: The approved inner-loop design dispatches each
canonical_claim: The approved inner-loop design dispatches each part's unchanged `stageManifest → precommitAdd → uploadPendingBlobs → promote` sequence to bounded workers, preserving per-part ordering while overlapping parts.

topic: The CAS commit pool must use
canonical_claim: The CAS commit pool must use bounded worker-loop callbacks or a dedicated pool sized by `cas_commit_concurrency`; scheduling one task per part on a shared 100-thread pool would not enforce the bound and could starve unrelated users.

topic: The initial multi-commit design used commitTransactions
canonical_claim: The initial multi-commit design used `commitTransactions` as a transaction-centric seam: generic implementations loop sequentially, while `MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts` groups same-disk transactions without leaking `isContentAddressed` checks into generic MergeTree code.

topic: Move assignment for PreparedPartWrite is deleted
canonical_claim: Move assignment for `PreparedPartWrite` is deleted because overwriting a handle that still owes a terminal action may require a fallible `abandon`, which move assignment cannot report without dropping cleanup ownership.

topic: The part-write release seam is relink-independent
canonical_claim: The part-write release seam is relink-independent: any `PartWriteTxn` may leave a staged precommit whose release is unproven, and the accounting is intentionally not attributed to relink or another consumer.

topic: ~PartWriteTxn, rather than ~PreparedPartWrite, owns the
canonical_claim: `~PartWriteTxn`, rather than `~PreparedPartWrite`, owns the final release word because `prepareEntries` can fail before constructing a handle; the transaction destructor therefore covers both handle and no-handle staging exits.

topic: Poisoned is not equivalent to a
canonical_claim: `Poisoned` is not equivalent to a wedge: it means a durable transaction may be missing from the cached view, so it continues to block snapshot publication and triggers re-recovery; making `ApplyPending` debug-only is a follow-up, not part of Stage B.

topic: The RemovalReady protocol is adopted as
canonical_claim: The `RemovalReady` protocol is adopted as a transient catalog state between `Removing` and entry deletion: it is entered only after the terminal record has folded and the life-scoped cleanup item is durably `Completed`.

topic: The final recommendation is to keep
canonical_claim: The final recommendation is to keep `NamespaceLifeId` and incarnation-qualified ref and namespace-file keys, avoid permanent `Retired` history and extra retirement markers, and delete a catalog entry only after terminal fold, cleanup/cursor retirement, and exact `_ckpt` deletion ordering is complete.

topic: The incarnation is retained because temporary
canonical_claim: The incarnation is retained because temporary refusal alone cannot make omitted old physical objects safe for eventual same-name reuse; the generation makes old ref objects and namespace files structurally inert.

topic: The RemovalReady state machine is Creating
canonical_claim: The `RemovalReady` state machine is `Creating -> Live -> Removing -> RemovalReady -> absent`; `RemovalReady` means no writer publication, recovery, ref fold, or new cursor is permitted, and only exact removal of the row is legal.

topic: The tokenless DETACH/freeze adopt path can
canonical_claim: The tokenless DETACH/freeze adopt path can race GC condemnation because `copyForwardFromCondemned` runs once before the CAS closure; the proposed fix is a bounded copy-forward and re-HEAD loop outside the closure, analogous to tokened resurrection.

topic: part lifecycle claim
canonical_claim: FREEZE uses one ref per frozen part rather than a shared container to avoid shared-`detached` read-modify-write and B66a torn-read hazards under concurrent freeze.

topic: part lifecycle claim
canonical_claim: Content-addressed storage requires a real transaction commit point, so `RegisterDiskObjectStorage.cpp` sets `needs_real_transaction=true` for CAS.

topic: part lifecycle claim
canonical_claim: The consistency review recommends using `TemporaryFileOnDisk` for CAS spill cleanup and considering `WriteBuffer`'s idempotent `finalize`/`cancel` state machine for the duplicated write-sink lifetime state.

topic: part lifecycle claim
canonical_claim: The `TXN-ONE-PIPELINE` design gives `IDiskTransaction::precommit` an explicit two-phase contract: CA precommit performs manifest publish through promote, CA commit materializes durable intent, and one `dispatch` funnel replaces the CA subclass.

topic: part lifecycle claim
canonical_claim: The T6 retirement fence is correct: slot retirement is forbidden while any entry owned by the root remains, so the proposed exemption for just-transitioned `Removing` rows was rejected.

topic: part lifecycle claim
canonical_claim: The optional age-based trickle warmer pushes blobs of hot parts older than a threshold `A` into the pool ahead of any snapshot, on the reasoning that a part surviving the young-merge window will likely reach the cold tier eventually; with the warmer on, consolidation degrades into publishing metadata only, and TTL moves become nearly free.

topic: part lifecycle claim
canonical_claim: `kMutablePerPartFiles` was renamed to `kPerRefPartFiles` (with per-file rationale documented): `txn_version.txt` is genuinely mutable in-place (MVCC rewrites it after part publication) and stays a per-ref mutable sidecar; `uuid.txt` and `metadata_version.txt` are not mutated in-place under the single-owner-manifest model and were reclassified as ordinary immutable part files inside the manifest rather than sidecars, since the old dual-part-ref-sharing-one-manifest rationale for excluding them no longer applies once CAS stages a fresh `ManifestId` per ref.

topic: part lifecycle claim
canonical_claim: Scenario S37 passed 22 of 23 verdicts; all non-MOVE multi-disk legs passed, including policy placement, insert-time `max_data_part_size` routing, truthful `disk_name`, restart re-attach, and mixed-disk merge, while only cross-disk `clonePart` to CA failed.

topic: part lifecycle claim
canonical_claim: Setting `alive = false` in `PartWriteTxn::promote` was rejected because existing promote-adjacent paths and the transaction destructor rely on current `abandon` no-op or soft-fail behavior.

topic: part lifecycle claim
canonical_claim: Nested sub-manifests per projection (each projection its own sub-PartManifest plus a projections footer) were rejected as a format/version change requiring a recursive resolver for identity projections never use, since projections are always read as children and rebuilt on merge (YAGNI). A separate projections/ ref namespace lifecycle-linked to the parent was also rejected as a second namespace plus GC coupling for no benefit.
